title: Dark text on dark background until settings are opened

judgment.rationale: The existing yellow-confidence candidate remains current: the reporter supplies a cold-start/settings-open comparison, but startup ordering has not been verified. The live discussion contains no comments or attachments; a prior artifact claim about a commenter was removed.
evidence: The reporter supplies a five-step cold-start sequence on preview 0.102.2883.0: Dark Dock text starts dark and changes to white when settings opens.
Changing background configuration did not remove the symptom.
The live issue has no comments or attachments; related issue 45998 concerns a different custom-background and Light-theme contrast case.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce startup event ordering, then consider a shared initial-and-change theme application path only if the missing initial synchronization is confirmed.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix, matching upstream PR, or issue-number-matched MuyuanMS/PowerToys issue/PR/branch trace was found. The candidate is limited to the source-supported startup theme synchronization boundary, not a general foreground contrast redesign.

proposed_fixes.title: Synchronize the Dock root theme when the Dock is first created
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a newly constructed Dock can inherit the application's theme until the next ThemeChanged callback, because its root receives the explicit Dock theme only in that callback. A startup snapshot/event ordering mismatch could therefore leave Dark Dock text using Light resources until settings opening causes a refresh.
plan: First record ThemeService.Initialize/Reload and DockWindow construction order on preview 0.102.2883.0 and current main, and inspect Root.RequestedTheme/ActualTheme before and after settings opening.

If that confirms an unsynchronized new root, in src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Dock/DockWindow.xaml.cs factor the existing root-theme application into one UI-thread method and invoke it after Root exists, using the current Dock theme snapshot; retain ThemeChanged updates.

Verify that a default Light snapshot cannot win over the subsequently loaded saved theme. Adjust initialization sequencing only if the observed event order requires it; do not hard-code white foreground or change contrast policy.
Add targeted startup and Dock-recreation coverage proving that explicit Dark/Light and system theme are applied before first visible content and continue to update after settings changes.
verification: Cold-start with Dock explicitly Dark while Windows/application theme is Light; text must be readable before opening settings and opening settings must not change it.
Repeat with explicit Light, system-following theme, alternate background configurations and High Contrast.
Recreate the Dock through its existing monitor/settings lifecycle and ensure theme state is preserved without waiting for a new global event.

confidence.rationale: The observed settings-open recovery and root-theme event-only assignment support this boundary, but no interactive reproduction or startup-order trace confirms it. Foreground resource initialization elsewhere remains a competing explanation.

issue_context.summary: A Dark Command Palette Dock initially has unreadable dark text after restart; merely opening Dock settings changes it to white. This differs from a permanently low-contrast custom background after switching to Light.
known_information: Reported preview version is 0.102.2883.0, installed through auto-update.
The body gives a five-step cold-start reproduction and says changing background configuration did not help.
There are no attachments or assignees. Labels are Issue-Bug and Needs-Triage.
Issue 45998 discusses automatic contrast for a custom background and a converter's background-image limitation; no fix is established there.
The current live issue has no comments or attachments; no additional reporter evidence was posted after the source timestamp.
inferences: A missing initial application of saved Dock theme is plausible, not a confirmed resource or timing root cause.
The settings-open transition is a useful discriminator against treating this as only custom-background contrast policy.
issue_context.analysis: The cold-start comparison remains sufficient for maintainer reproduction. Startup theme/resource ordering is a hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause; keep the specific reproduction action paired with the yellow plan.
initial_investigation: Inspected DockWindow.xaml, DockWindow.xaml.cs, ThemeService.cs, DockWindowManager.cs and DockWindowViewModel.cs at upstream main 1b33221dfa19f30d71409eb550807883fb27283a.

Root has no explicit RequestedTheme in XAML. DockWindow's change callback applies Dark, then Light, then CurrentDockTheme.Theme to refresh resources; a corresponding initial root assignment was not found in its construction sequence.
ThemeService starts with a Light Dock snapshot; Reload computes the effective saved theme and raises ThemeChanged. The actual order relative to Dock construction has not been measured.
No cross-reference timeline entries or matching upstream issue-number PRs were found; the focused open Dock-theme PR search also returned none.
No matching issue, PR or branch-ref trace was found in MuyuanMS/PowerToys. No canonical main artifact exists for this number.

actions.label: Reproduce Dark Dock startup theme ordering

prerequisites: Official preview 0.102.2883.0 when available; compare a current-main development build.
Enable the Dock and save explicit Dark Dock appearance; use Windows/application Light theme to distinguish inherited from Dock-specific theme.
steps: 1. Exit and restart PowerToys/Command Palette without opening any settings.
2. Record text appearance and, in a debug build, Root.RequestedTheme, Root.ActualTheme and CurrentDockTheme.Theme at Dock creation and first display.
3. Open Dock settings without changing a value; record the same values and whether text immediately changes.

4. Record ordering of ThemeService.Initialize/Reload and ThemeChanged subscription relative to InitializeComponent; determine whether the saved-theme event precedes creation or whether a resource refresh is missed.
5. Repeat with Dock Light, system-following appearance, a different background configuration, and a recreated Dock. Test High Contrast before implementation approval.
reproduce.expected: The saved Dock appearance is reflected on first display; merely opening settings produces no corrective foreground change.
